resources.string: Second screen for the AYN Thor
One tap: finds the PC on your network, works out which game it\'s running, and opens the second screen.
Set the address by hand, choose the display, and control how the screen behaves.
Needs the Ayn Dual Screen SMAPI mod. Network access is on by default; if it was turned off, set \"AllowLanAccess\": true in its config.json.
Needs the Ayn Dual Screen tModLoader mod. Network access is on by default; if it was turned off, re-enable AllowLanAccess in its mod config.

Needs the Ayn Dual Screen Forge mod for Minecraft 1.21.1. It uses port 27302 so it doesn\'t clash with the other two. Network access is on by default; if it was turned off, set allowLanAccess = true in config/ayndualscreen-client.toml.
Keep retrying when the game restarts. Off: drop straight back to the menu when the session ends.
Reopen on the same panel next time without asking.
Hold the screen on. Turning this off lets the panel dim normally.
Found %1$d. Tap one to use it.
Nothing found on port %1$d. Check the game is running with LAN access on, and that a VPN isn\'t in the way.
Connected to %1$s, but it\'s at the main menu. Load a save and the screen will fill in.
That address is running %1$s, not %2$s. Switch the game above, or check the address.
Something answered there, but it isn\'t one of the mods. %1$s
The PC is there, but nothing is listening on that port. %1$s is either not running, or the mod is still on localhost only — enable LAN access in the mod and restart the game.
That address doesn\'t resolve. Try the PC\'s numeric IP from \"ipconfig\" instead of its name.
No answer. The address may be on a different network, or Windows Firewall may be blocking the port — allow it for Private networks.

\"localhost\" means this device, not your PC — that\'s why it fails here. The mod prints that address for use on the PC itself. Enter the PC\'s network address instead, from \"ipconfig\" (it looks like 192.168.x.x).
Enter the PC\'s address first, or tap Find my PC.
The game session closed — back to the menu.
Couldn\'t get the session back — back to the menu.
Couldn\'t load the wiki. It needs an internet connection.

Needs the Ayn Dual Screen xNVSE plugin, and the game started through nvse_loader.exe rather than FalloutNV.exe — launched directly, the plugin never loads. It uses port 27303. Network access is on by default; if it was turned off, set AllowLanAccess=1 in Data\\NVSE\\Plugins\\AynDualScreen.ini. Tale of Two Wastelands works with the same plugin.
Any web page, opened full-screen with no browser chrome. Handy for a dashboard, a stream, or a wiki parked on the second display.
Looking for a game on your network…
No game found. Pick one and enter its address.
On launch, check the saved address and switch to whatever is actually running.
Dress the home screen as a handheld. Tap one to switch; tap Ayn Dual Screen to go back to the app\'s own look.
A theme is one small JSON file, plus a folder of PNG icons if you want them. Every field is optional. The quickest way to get files onto the device is this app\'s own FTP server.
Ready: %1$s\n\nexample.json and README.txt are in there. Copy the example, rename it, and it appears in this list.
Could not create the folder. Grant all-files access on the FTP screen first.
Not finished — the app can pair with a PC, but nothing decodes video yet.

Pairs this device with a PC running Sunshine or GeForce Experience. Pairing works and is remembered — but nothing decodes video yet, so there is no game to watch here. This is the groundwork, not the feature.
Paired — this PC knows this device.
Something is already streaming from this PC.
Sunshine shows a PIN page in its web interface. GeForce Experience pops up a box on the desktop.
Needs a companion program on the PC — not built yet.
Shares this device over the network so a PC can browse and copy its files, the way ftpd does on a 3DS. Plain FTP, on your own network — no encryption.
Server is off. Start it, then type this address into your PC\'s file manager.
Start the server when the app opens
The server is not running. Go back and press Start server.
Go back, change the port if that is the problem, and try again. If this keeps happening, the message above is the exact reason — send it on.
The server is running, but this device has no address a PC could reach. Connect to Wi-Fi.
Anonymous — any username and password will do.
FTP sends the password in clear text. It is a doorlock for your own network, not a secret — don\'t reuse a real one.
Anything worth keeping to hand: seed numbers, boss order, a shopping list.
Applies while the app is open, and needs no permission.
Changes device brightness for everything. Needs the Modify System Settings permission.
Android has no public way to set two panels separately, so this moves both.
Every change lands here as you make it
A whole look in one tap. Everything below still works afterwards.
Hide the ones you never use. They stay off the home grid until you turn them back on.
Take this off the home grid? You can bring it back under Appearance → Tools shown.
Not enabled yet. Turn it on in the system keyboard list, then come back and switch to it.
Enabled, but not the one in use. Tap Switch to it and pick Thor Keyboard.
Active. It\'s the keyboard everything on this device now types with.
Split pushes the keys out to the edges, under your thumbs, the way a handheld wants them. Full width uses the whole row.
Type here with the keys below
Copies this device\'s main screen onto its second panel, and keeps going while you use other apps. It shows the Thor\'s own screen — not the PC\'s.
Mirroring. The second panel is showing this screen; stop it here or from the notification.
Ready. Android will ask you to confirm screen capture before it starts.
Screen capture was declined, so nothing is being mirrored.
No second display found. Plug one in, or open the Thor\'s second panel, then come back.
Needs permission to draw over other apps — that\'s what puts the picture on the second panel while you\'re in a game.
Floating buttons that stay on screen while you use other apps. Text and key macros go through the Thor Keyboard, so they land wherever you\'re typing — they can\'t reach a game\'s own controls.
Delete \"%1$s\" and every button in it?
This is the only profile left. Make another one first.
No buttons in this profile yet.
What it says on the button
Hidden. Show it and the buttons stay put while you use anything else.
On screen. Tap a button to fire it.
Moving. Drag the buttons where you want them — they save as you drop them.
Needs permission to draw over other apps, which is what keeps the buttons on screen outside this app.
Switch to the Thor Keyboard first — that\'s what puts the text in.
Couldn\'t find an app with package %1$s.
Tap Hide to put it away.
